attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the softened 'kind of look the same' and the detail defects. It is an aesthetic observation with no defined standard.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds that no whole-claim test exists without adding definitions of sameness, which models count, and what level of detail is acceptable. Treating it as not_applicable is fair.

evidence.note: HEIM is a 2023 benchmark that scores separate dimensions. It does not measure the qualified aesthetic judgment as a whole.

reviews.rationale: This is a vague, softened aesthetic judgment ('kind of look the same', details 'look off') with no measurable standard. The contract can specify no support or contradiction condition, and the benchmark is context only. It cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion, followed by examples he chose.

semantics.note: The statement says there are many stories about the technology's unreliability, and the speaker endorses that. The normalisation is slightly firmer but acceptable, since the contract reads it as documented incidents rather than a failure rate.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: multiple documented incidents of faulty generative-AI output before the post. It does not require a population-wide failure rate.

evidence.note: A June 2023 court finding that ChatGPT fabricated case citations.
A January 2024 TIME report of the DPD chatbot misbehaving, with DPD confirming it disabled the AI. This is a separate incident in a different setting.
FinanceBench (November 2023) found weaknesses, including hallucinations, in all 16 model configurations it tested.

reviews.rationale: A court record, independent reporting and an academic evaluation, all dated before the post, document incorrect or inappropriate generative-AI outputs in distinct settings. That meets the support condition, and nothing in the packet contradicts it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The scare-quoted 'improve' is his own framing.

semantics.note: The proposition is faithful to the statement, including the spending premise and 'few ways'. The concession that models 'might improve' is not scored.

contract.note: Reading 'few ways' as limited practical mitigation is reasonable. Still, the result depends on undefined terms ('few ways', 'intellect') and on a spending basis the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of halving false statements. It is a self-report, not an independent finding, and it covers only one firm without settling 'few ways'.
OpenAI's own disclosure that hallucinations persist. It gives no measure of how much mitigation happened and says nothing about spending.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only company self-disclosures pointing in different directions. It has no comparable evaluation across the three firms and no spending evidence on a matching basis. The evidence does not settle whether mitigation was 'few'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will always cost less' is a firm, permanent forecast that the cost ordering will hold. It is correctly captured, with no deadline.

contract.note: Given the post's cloud-provider framing, the provider-side cost reading is fair. The early-resolution rule, which needs a reproducible counterexample, is reasonable.

evidence.note: Compares user-paid mobile data plus token prices, not provider serving costs. It fails the contract's cost boundary, so it cannot trigger early resolution.

reviews.rationale: A permanent forecast with no deadline. The only evidence uses a user-cost boundary, which does not meet the contradiction condition, so no conclusive event has occurred. Finite observations cannot confirm 'always'.
